signal.sound-multi: Several tones at once or jumping quickly
signal.empty: No mode matches these filters. Contradictory answers have no solution; change one of them and try again — this page does not guess the closest match.
signal.cw-hint: Keyed tones with a pitch, uneven length, clear gaps between letters and words; with a narrow filter almost a single tone.
signal.rtty-hint: Two alternating tones chirping at a mechanical, even rate; 170 Hz shift, about 250 Hz wide.
signal.psk31-hint: A thin, slightly wavering whistle that stops and starts as someone types slowly, with almost no idle gaps.
signal.ft8-hint: A short burst of several tones every 15 seconds lasting about 12.6 seconds, then silence.
signal.ft4-hint: A multi-tone burst every 7.5 seconds — twice the pace of FT8 and slightly wider.
signal.wspr-hint: A very narrow four-tone whistle every 2 minutes at low level; often only audible through a narrow filter.
signal.olivia-hint: Continuous multi-tone hiss several hundred Hz wide, sounding like a steady band of noise rather than a tone.
signal.dominoex-hint: Continuous fast multi-tone jumping, grainier than Olivia and more granular to the ear.
signal.hell-hint: Rhythmic pulses on a single tone, like a buzzing machine, with a speed set by the sender.
signal.navtex-hint: Narrow two-tone FSK carrying continuous maritime bulletins, usually on medium wave and marine HF frequencies.
signal.packet-hint: A two-tone burst under a second, then long silence; APRS often shares a voice repeater's frequency.
signal.sstv-hint: Over a minute of continuous sweeping tones like an old fax machine, repeating after each picture.
signal.wefax-hint: Minutes of hiss with periodic sync pulses — this is what HF weather fax sounds like.
signal.apt-hint: Wideband hiss about 40 kHz wide, present only during the few minutes of a satellite pass.
signal.ssb-hint: Speech that is muffled and thin; tuned a few hundred Hz off it turns into a duck-like quack.
signal.fm-hint: Clear speech over a clean noise floor; when weak the noise suddenly rises instead of gradually blurring.
signal.lora-hint: Wideband chirps sweeping from low to high within a second; far wider than any voice mode.
signal.unknown-hint: No entry in the feature table.
